benefits: Converts any raw score into a universal z-score in one step.
Shows the percentile and both tail probabilities automatically.
No z-table lookup needed — the normal CDF is computed precisely.
Ideal for exam scores, quality control and standardized testing.
Runs fully in your browser; your data stays private.

faqs.a: A z-score measures how many standard deviations a value sits from the mean: z = (x − μ) / σ. A z of 0 means exactly average; +2 means two standard deviations above the mean.
Roughly speaking, yes for bell-shaped data: about 68% of values have |z| < 1, 95% have |z| < 2, and 99.7% have |z| < 3. A z beyond ±3 is genuinely unusual.
The percentile is Φ(z) × 100 — the percentage of a normal distribution at or below your value. A z of 1.5 gives the 93.32nd percentile: about 93.3% of values fall below.

They can, but the percentile interpretation assumes a normal distribution. For heavily skewed data the z-score is still a valid standardized distance, but percentiles should be read from the data itself.
faqs.q: Can I use z-scores on non-normal data?

faqs.a: Yes. A negative z-score simply means the value is below the mean — for example z = −1.2 means 1.2 standard deviations below average.

z-score-calculator.formula:
z = (x − μ) / σ

x = your value, μ = mean, σ = standard deviation

Percentile = Φ(z) × 100, where Φ is the standard normal CDF:
Φ(z) = (1 / √(2π)) ∫₋∞ᵗ e^(−t²/2) dt

The tool evaluates Φ with a high-precision rational approximation
(error below 7.5 × 10⁻⁸), so no table lookup is needed.
howTo: Enter your value x — the score you want to standardize.
Enter the mean μ of the distribution it comes from.
Enter the standard deviation σ (it must be greater than zero).
Read the z-score: positive means above average, negative below.
Check the percentile and the probabilities of scoring below or above x.
keyFacts: A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean: z = (x − μ) / σ.
Z-scores are unitless, so scores from different tests become comparable.
The percentile Φ(z) × 100 tells you what share of values fall below yours.
For normal data, |z| > 3 happens only about 0.3% of the time.
Standard deviation must be positive — with σ = 0 every value equals the mean.
z-score-calculator.keywords: z-score calculator, standard score calculator, z score to percentile, normal distribution calculator

labels.invalidNote: Standard deviation must be greater than zero.

limitations: Percentiles assume a normal (bell-shaped) distribution — check this for your data.
The z-score cannot fix bad data: garbage inputs give precise-looking garbage.
σ = 0 is rejected; a constant dataset has no meaningful z-scores.
The normal CDF is approximated (error < 7.5×10⁻⁸) — exact enough for all practical use.

z-score-calculator.quickAnswer: Enter a value, mean and standard deviation — for example x = 85, μ = 70, σ = 10 gives z = 1.5, the 93.32nd percentile, P(X ≤ 85) ≈ 0.9332 and P(X > 85) ≈ 0.0668.
z-score-calculator.tagline: Standard score, percentile and normal probabilities from any value.
z-score-calculator.workedExample:
Exam score x = 85, class mean μ = 70, SD σ = 10:
z = (85 − 70) / 10 = 15 / 10 = 1.5

The score is 1.5 standard deviations above the mean.
Φ(1.5) ≈ 0.9332 → 93.32nd percentile
P(X ≤ 85) ≈ 0.9332 — about 93.3% of students scored 85 or less
P(X > 85) ≈ 0.0668 — about 6.7% scored higher
